messages:
Leila Farouk: heads up: E2E staging test `dedicated_staged_rollout_gate_fail_then_approve` is stuck between stages again. It creates plan, enters Stage 1 (5%), gates pass, I click approve for Stage 2 and it never advances. UI shows “Awaiting advancement” forever. Anyone around to debug?

Hannah Rivera: yup seeing the same in Console. Stage 1 shows green, Stage 2 shows “Pending” but the banner says “Approved”. It’s like we recorded the approval but the state machine didn’t move.

Benji Okafor: can you drop rollout_id + pool_id from staging?

Leila Farouk: rollout_id `rpl_7c3f9a1e` (tenant `tnt_staging-enterprise-12`), pool `ded-pool-stg-04`. route `chat/completions` model `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`.

Chloe Martin: checking console-backend logs (stg) for `rpl_7c3f9a1e`.

Chloe Martin: found this around the approve click:
```
service=console-rollouts api=POST /v1/dedicated/rollouts/rpl_7c3f9a1e/approve actor=hannah.rivera stage=stage-2 plan_version=12
msg="approval accepted" approval_id=apv_1f29
```
Then polling status keeps returning:
```
current_stage_id=stage-1 current_stage_state=COMPLETE
next_stage_id=stage-2 next_stage_state=PENDING
pending_transition="ADVANCE_STAGE" approved=true
```

Jada Williams: that “pending_transition” should clear on evaluator tick. maybe evaluator saw it but bailed?

Benji Okafor: grabbing control-plane logs for evaluator (stg). one sec.

Benji Okafor: ok I see a suspicious optimistic concurrency fail:
```
svc=rollout-evaluator env=staging rollout_id=rpl_7c3f9a1e tick=2024-12-09T19:12:41Z
msg="attempting stage advance" from_stage=stage-1 to_stage=stage-2 plan_version=12

svc=rollout-evaluator
msg="update failed" err="OptimisticLockError: expected plan_version=12 got=13" op="SetCurrentStage(stage-2)"

svc=rollout-evaluator
msg="will retry next tick" backoff="none"
```
It never succeeds after that; every tick says expected 12 got 13, then expected 13 got 14, etc.

Michael Nguyen: wait plan_version incrementing every tick? that sounds like something is writing the plan row repeatedly (even on no-op) and bumping version.

Ethan Park: +1. plan_version should only bump on plan mutations (edit stages/gates) or when we write state transitions if we’re using same version field for both config + state. are we?

Benji Okafor: in current schema we used `plan_version` as the row version for the whole RolloutPlan record (config + state machine fields). Evaluator does `UPDATE ... WHERE version = ?` and increments version. Console polling might also be touching it?

Chloe Martin: console backend does a `touch_last_viewed_at` on read for now (to power “recent rollouts” list ordering). I think it updates the same row. :facepalm:

Hannah Rivera: lol that would explain version churn while UI is open + polling.

Jordan Lee: yep, if read-path is updating the same versioned row, the CAS in evaluator will basically never win under frequent polling. especially with websocket fallback to 2s poll.

Jada Williams: we need to stop writing on GET, or move that recency field out of the plan row (separate table keyed by actor/tenant?)

Michael Nguyen: quick fix: make the `last_viewed_at` update not bump the optimistic concurrency version (either separate column not part of CAS, or separate table). Depending on ORM, easiest might be to move it to a different table `rollout_plan_views(rollout_id, actor_id, last_viewed_at)`.

Ravi Menon: + we should not couple config versioning with state transitions anyway. we’ll keep hitting similar races (approval arrives + evaluator tick). should have state transitions on separate state record with its own locking.

Ethan Park: agreed longer-term. for this staging blocker: can we remove the “touch” write entirely? We don’t need it for beta.

Chloe Martin: I can patch console-backend today to stop the `touch_last_viewed_at` write on GET /status and only do it on list page (and even there, maybe client-side). That should stop version churn.

Benji Okafor: that should fix “stuck between stages” for now. but we should also harden evaluator retry logic: on OptimisticLockError, re-read and if approved + still on same stage, retry with latest version *immediately*, not wait 30s tick.

Jordan Lee: +1. and we should ensure the evaluator advance is idempotent (if someone else advanced, just exit clean).

DeployBot: Deploy requested by Chloe Martin to staging: `console-rollouts-backend` branch `cm/no-touch-on-status` (build #18422)

Leila Farouk: while that’s deploying, here are the evaluator tick lines showing constant failure (last 5 mins):
```
19:13:11 OptimisticLockError expected=13 got=14
19:13:41 OptimisticLockError expected=14 got=15
19:14:11 OptimisticLockError expected=15 got=16
19:14:41 OptimisticLockError expected=16 got=17
19:15:11 OptimisticLockError expected=17 got=18
```
So yeah, something is bumping version on basically every poll cycle.

Chloe Martin: staging deploy is live. I disabled the write on status reads + turned down polling on detail page from 2s -> 10s while websocket is connected.

Hannah Rivera: retesting on the same rollout_id (still in that state). I reloaded the page, clicked “Re-evaluate gates” (no-op), then approve Stage 2 again.

Benji Okafor: watching evaluator logs…

Benji Okafor: nice, it advanced on next tick:
```
msg="attempting stage advance" from_stage=stage-1 to_stage=stage-2 version=19
msg="stage advanced" new_current_stage=stage-2 version=20
```

Leila Farouk: E2E test passed after rerun. :thumbsup: marking flaky fixed. Can we file follow-up for splitting config version vs state + fixing retry?

Ethan Park: yep. I’ll open an eng issue: (1) stop touching plan row on reads everywhere (2) separate state record + lease/lock for stage advancement (3) evaluator immediate retry on lock fail. This is exactly the kind of “stuck between stages” we can’t ship.

Jordan Lee: also add an alert for “approval exists but stage doesn’t advance within X mins” (could be evaluator lag / lock contention). SRE will want that.

Michael Nguyen: I’ll add a migration note: if we keep `plan_version` for config, we should add `state_version` for transitions. Otherwise any UI write path can break us again.

Chloe Martin: I’ll link this thread + the patch diff in the PR description. thanks all.
